verdict.rationale: Cline's own docs say it runs long-running dev servers live, reacts to terminal output as it appears, and can use a browser, with browser actions listed among the actions it can take. Together these give a basic way to run and inspect a live web app from the assistant, but the docs never describe a dedicated live-debugging workflow. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of debugging a running web app (e.g. console/network log inspection, breakpoints or debugger attach), a worked example of a live debug loop, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug a live running web application directly from my coding assistant

citations.quote: Executes in your terminal and reacts to output as it appears. Long-running dev servers, tests, deploys, all handled live.
It can read and write files, run terminal commands, use a browser, and help you build features through natural conversation.
Cline auto-approves everything: file changes, terminal commands, browser actions, MCP tools, and mode transitions.
